variants.asks: the settled vacuum has room ahead of every ray, and the world grows only where a ray has nowhere to step. How fast does it grow, then?

steps.because: the rules, read as a line: every rule of the theory is a term, the reading having run each rule's program on a symbolic match and counted what it does to the population - what it makes, what it takes, what it carries, what a body puts in - so the line is what the rules come to as a crowd rather than a description of them. Everything a theorem of this theory stands on is a term of this line or a reading of one, so every premise below is read off it, and every derivation passes through it

derivation.because: ANNIHILATION contributes it: its body comes to -2 rays and -1 points of space, its quantifier makes it of degree 2 in the density across an edge, which is the facing factor, and its gates let through what they let through

rule /1 "Annihilation" | σ (x: 1 Edge{active}) => x.ANNIHILATE - -2 rays, -1 points of space. The reading follows the body down through the methods it calls, and the ledgers it moves are counted off the assignments it makes

the rule is quantified over 2 population-bearing refs, so its term carries the density to the power 2 - and the two are across an edge, so the rate goes against the oncoming current, which is the facing factor F
the rule fires only where active, so whatever it does it does on that share of its matches and the term carries it

the rules do not consult one another - each fires on its own matches once a tick - so what they do to the population adds, and the line is what they come to rather than a description of them. A theory with a rule taken out writes one term fewer here without anything else changing

steps.via: the world grows at its frontier
working: at the frontier: MOVEMENT at 1 - \omega, one cell a tick
steps.because: so what grows the world is the frontier alone: a ray with nowhere to step makes the room and steps into it, the same tick - a ray never waits. The frontier advances a cell a tick, so a world grown from a point is as wide as it is old, R = \bar{c}t, and its rate of growth is one over its age: H = \dot{R}/R = 1/t. It is not a constant: it thins as the world ages, a coasting expansion, and today it is one over the age

working: MOVEMENT grows at 1 - \omega: nought where every ray has room ahead
derivation.because: the growth ledger read where the vacuum has settled: every ray there has room ahead, so MOVEMENT grows nothing and no meeting leaves a point behind a vacuum ray. The empty vacuum grows no space of its own - there is no constant in these rules that thins nothing

a firing that makes a point no local held - behind a ray at a meeting, ahead of a ray with nowhere to step - grows the world by it, at its own rate, through its own gates, the count written on it. This is the room the world gains per local per tick: what it expands by
